newsitem.title: USA: U.S. asks Russia to waive diplomat's immunity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. asks Russia to waive diplomat's immunity.

text.p: The United States has asked Russia to waive the diplomatic immunity of one of its diplomats in Washington involved in an alleged drunk-driving case last weekend, the State Department said on Thursday.
Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Vadim Savelyev, a second secretary and vice-consul, was given three citations after being stopped by police last Sunday near Annapolis, Maryland.
They were for driving at 76 mph (120 km/h) in a 55 mph (90 km/h) zone, for making an unsafe lane change and for driving while intoxicated, Burns told reporters.

Asked if U.S. authorities had asked Russia to waive Savelyev's immunity so that he could face prosecution, Burns said: "That's standard procedure." But he said he did not know what if any response there had been from Russia.
The case followed that of Georgian diplomat Gueorgui Makharadze, whose immunity was waived by his government after he was involved in a car crash that killed a teenage girl in Washington in January.
Makharadze pleaded innocent to charges of involuntary manslaughter and aggravated assault and was scheduled to be tried starting July 21.
